evidence: Receiving DO2 falls from 10.75 mg/L at t=48.0 h to 2.43 mg/L at t=48.2 h and declines to 1.64 mg/L by t=52.0 h (simulated_online_sensor)
Receiving P assay: 0.0 g/L at 24 h, 1.03 g/L at 36 h, 3.04 g/L at 48 h (simulated_delayed_assay) — production ramp coincides with DO crash
Source batches 1–3 sustain DO ~8–10 mg/L at t=48–52 h while producing ~3 g/L, showing receiving transfer capacity differs from source
minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0; current receiving DO of 1.64 mg/L is below the constraint under KEEP
Allowed action bounds: strong_feed_reduction = [0.6 feed, 1.15 air]
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 crashed at 48.2 h from ~11 mg/L to ~2.4 mg/L and has drifted to 1.64 mg/L at the 52 h decision point, already below the 2.0 mg/L minimum oxygen constraint. The crash coincides with the product-formation ramp (P: 1.03 -> 3.04 g/L between 36 h and 48 h), indicating feed-driven oxygen demand exceeding the receiving vessel's transfer capacity. KEEP would prolong the constraint violation; increase_air alone cannot close a ~5x DO deficit; combined (0.8/1.15) leaves little margin above the 2.0 floor given the downward trend. Stop yields zero counted production. strong_feed_reduction (0.6 feed, 1.15 air) most aggressively removes the oxygen-demand driver while raising transfer, restoring DO compliance while retaining product mass and continued production.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving-process kinetics mean the DO response to feed reduction may lag; if recovery is slow, production rate will be lower than under combined, creating a modest yield cost. The 1.64 mg/L reading could include sensor noise, but the entire 48.2-52.0 h window sits at ~1.6-2.9 mg/L, so the breach is robust. No extra assay requested because the online DO evidence is timely and decisive, and a 4 h assay turnaround would delay intervention during an ongoing oxygen-constraint violation.

evidence: Source batches (source-1/2/3) maintained DO2 ~9–10 mg/L over 48–52 h, showing the receiving oxygen collapse is process-specific (estimated transfer multiplier 0.434, change ~48 h)
Delayed product assays (receiving): P(12h)=0.06, P(24h)=0.0, P(36h)=1.03, P(48h)=3.04 g/L — substantial accumulated product argues against stop

Forward model comparison at 52 h: strong_feed_reduction min DO 1.13 mg/L, oxygen deficit 4.32 mg·h/L, product mass 172.3 kg vs keep (1.01, 5.42, 171.3), increase_air (0.87, 8.67, 171.3), combined (0.96, 6.88, 171.4), reduce_feed (0.85, 8.67, 171.3)
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at t≈48 h from ~10.7 to ~1.6–2.9 mg/L, at/below the 2.0 mg/L limit, while source batches sustained ~9–10 mg/L — indicating a receiving-specific oxygen-transfer deficit (model-estimated multiplier ~0.43). Air increase alone is insufficient (model: min DO 0.87, largest deficit). The strongest bounded feed reduction (0.6 feed + 1.15 air) minimizes oxygen demand and deficit (4.32 vs 5.42 keep), yields the highest predicted product mass (172.3 kg), and avoids a stop, which would zero counted production.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; across its sensitivity members no action achieves full feasibility (min DO 0.73–1.72 for strong_feed_reduction), so the improvement is partial. Timing of collapse and assay lag (4 h) limit knowledge of current product trajectory; feed reduction may somewhat slow further product accumulation versus keep.
